about.title: Private PDF tools for everyday work
about.intro: PagodaPDF is a browser-based PDF toolkit focused on useful document actions without forcing your files through an upload-first workflow. It is being adapted as an open source project with a lighter, cleaner interface.
about.localDescription: Core PDF actions run in the browser whenever possible, keeping documents on your device.
about.openDescription: The source can be reviewed, modified, and shared under the AGPL-3.0 license.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy

security.title: Protect & Encrypt PDFs
security.intro: Password encryption, digital signatures, permissions, and sensitive-data cleanup.
security.introStrong: 100% secure local processing in your browser (client-side WASM)
security.introEnd: Your documents are never uploaded to a server.
security.toolsDescription: Choose a tool to encrypt, unlock, or clean your PDF.
security.architectureTitle: Why Does Client-Side-Only Architecture Matter for Security?
security.architectureDescription: Most online tools upload private documents to third-party servers. PagodaPDF processes them locally instead.
security.legacyRiskOne: Contracts and financial reports are uploaded to an external server.
security.legacyRiskTwo: Data may leak if the server is attacked or stores activity logs.
security.legacyRiskThree: Large files depend on network upload and download speed.
security.localOne: 100% processed in your computer's memory through WebAssembly.
security.localTwo: Files never leave the browser, removing the risk of server-side exposure.
security.localThree: Fast processing that continues to work without an internet connection.
security.aesDescription: Use strong encryption to protect PDF contents.
security.signatureDescription: Create electronic signatures that verify document integrity and origin.
security.cleanupDescription: Remove hidden data, GPS locations, author details, and editing history.
security.freeDescription: No fixed file-size or daily usage limits.
security.faqDescription: Common answers about document encryption and security.
security.passwordQuestion: How do I password-protect a PDF?
security.passwordAnswer: Open Encrypt PDF, select your file, and enter a password. You can set a user password for opening the file and an owner password for print or editing permissions.
security.storageQuestion: Does PagodaPDF really avoid storing my files?
security.storageAnswer: Yes. PagodaPDF uses WebAssembly in your browser. Your files stay on your device, with no intermediary server involved in encryption or decryption.
security.flattenQuestion: How does Flatten PDF improve security?
security.flattenAnswer: Flattening combines interactive form fields, signatures, and annotations into fixed page content. This makes the document harder to alter and prevents signatures from being extracted as separate objects.
security.unlockQuestion: Can I unlock a PDF if I forgot the password?
security.unlockAnswer: Owner-password permission restrictions can often be removed with Decrypt PDF. For an AES-256 user password that protects file opening, you must provide the correct password.
